The family life cycle concept describes the typical stages families go through over time, from formation (marriage) to dissolution (death of a spouse), including phases such as having children, launching children, and retirement.  
This matches option (B), which directly captures the idea of family formation and dissolution.  
Option (A) is incorrect because, while psychographics may use family life cycle stages, the concept itself is not defined as a way to apply psychographics.  
Option (C) describes demographic interrelationships but is too narrow and not the core definition.  
Option (D) refers more to individual life stages, not the family unit over time.  

Final answer: (B)
